body:
Deleting a terminal buffer immediately after chansend() hangs Neovim with the standalone reproduction below.

Opening a separate issue as requested by the maintainers in #15349. The reproduction and investigation were first posted in https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/15349#issuecomment-6353852561.

## Environment

Reproduced on Linux with:

- Neovim 0.12.6
- Neovim 0.13.0-dev-1805+g39a740aaa7

No plugins or user configuration are required.

## Reproduction

Save as repro.lua:

```lua
  local job = vim.fn.jobstart({
    '/bin/sh', '-c', 'printf "ready\\n"; exec cat',
  }, { term = true })

  assert(job > 0)
  assert(vim.wait(1000, function()
    return vim.api.nvim_buf_get_lines(0, 0, 1, false)[1] == 'ready'
  end))

  -- Write and delete before libuv completes the write.
  vim.fn.chansend(job, 'pending write\n')
  vim.api.nvim_buf_delete(0, { force = true })

  -- Process queued events immediately after deletion.
  vim.wait(1, function() return false end)

  io.stdout:write('terminal deletion completed\n')
  vim.cmd('qa!')
```

Run with an external timeout; vim.wait() does not return during the hang:

```sh
  timeout -k 1s 3s nvim --headless -u NONE -i NONE \
    --noplugin -n -l repro.lua
```

Expected: prints terminal deletion completed and exits.

Actual: prints nothing and hangs until forcibly killed. This occurred in all three attempts on each unpatched build.

## Investigation

Interrupting the development build in a debugger produced this stack:

```text
  multiqueue_put_event
  term_delayed_free
  multiqueue_process_events
  nlua_loop_poll
```

term_delayed_free requeues itself onto chan->events while terminal I/O remains pending. The event processor keeps draining that queue, preventing libuv from running the callback that clears the pending write.

The same retry remains in upstream channel.c at d714648b8e7c.

## Candidate fix

The local change is:

```diff
  -    multiqueue_put(chan->events, term_delayed_free, chan);
  +    loop_schedule_deferred(&main_loop, event_create(term_delayed_free, chan));
```

The local patched build completed the reproduction in all three attempts, taking 27–29 ms.

This appears to let libuv make progress before cleanup retries. The pending-I/O checks and explicit reference-count operations are unchanged, but shutdown behavior, event ordering, and cross-platform safety still need validation.

PR #32755 addressed similar same-queue rescheduling in emit_termrequest; this reproduction reaches the separate cleanup path in channel.c.

title: Terminal buffer deletion hangs with a pending write
